paper.core_task: Evaluating motion utilization in video referring segmentation by video MLLMs

contributions.name: A motion-centric probing and benchmark for video MLLMs
contributions.author_claim_text: We create a motion-centric probing and evaluation technique that questions previous efforts on motion referring expressions segmentation and can be used to drive better understanding of video MLLMs performance.
contributions.description: The authors introduce a novel benchmark and probing method that pairs a static keyframe with the original video to test whether models rely on static cues instead of true motion for segmentation.

contributions.name: Strong single-image and semi-temporal baselines for referring video segmentation
contributions.author_claim_text: We establish strong single-image and semi-temporal baselines for referring video segmentation using powerful multi-modal large language models that can visually ground objects on the region level.
contributions.description: The paper proposes three baselines using MLLMs like Qwen2.5-VL with SAM/SAM 2.0 that outperform state-of-the-art methods despite being biased to static information.

contributions.name: Analysis of motion expression properties using GPT-4o
contributions.author_claim_text: We take another step to study both the dynamic and static cues conveyed from the referred motion expressions from the identified two groups.
contributions.description: The authors use GPT-4o to analyze properties like multi-step actions and dynamic verb phrases in referring expressions, distinguishing dynamic from static groups.

novelty_claims.text: The paper lacks a dedicated section outlining its contributions and novelty, which limits the clarity of its impact on the field.
The paper does not provide direct comparisons to existing benchmarks or methods, such as DAVIS'17 or other MLLMs, to demonstrate the novelty and effectiveness of the proposed approach.
